description.narrative:
The drought crisis in Somalia has reached alarming levels in 2025. The country is grappling with severe drought, erratic rainfall, and ongoing conflict, which have collectively pushed millions towards extreme hunger and malnutrition. Nearly 4.4 million people are food insecure, almost a quarter of the population, are expected to face crisis levels of food insecurity between April and June 2025 as per latest food security outlook projections. Approximately 1.7 million children under five are projected tosuffer from acute malnutrition, with 466,000 experiencing severe acute malnutrition. The drought has severely depleted water sources, leading to widespread waterborne diseases and forcing many to undertake exhausting journeys in search of water. This hasled many HHs to leave their homes in search of food and water.
Probable Development in 2025: Bay region including Burhakaba will Continue to remain dry and Drought expected to persist, the upcoming Gu season (April–June) is forecasted to be drier thannormal, likely leading to further crop failures and worsening food insecurity. There is an urgent need for a multi-sector approach combining immediate food security addressed as part of humanitarian aid response in Bay region combined with long term agricultural solutions to the target communities. The situation is dire, but with coordinated efforts, there is hope for alleviating some of the suffering.
This proposed project intendsto provide Multi purpose cash assistance to 842 Drought affected vulnerable displaced households Burhakaba districts in Bay region with three months of multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA). The MPCA will enable 5052 people (842HHs) affected population to meet their basic needs. The proposed intervention will target the most vulnerable HHs who need urgent lifesaving support in the targeted IDP sites. The MPCA beneficiaries will be selected based on the following criteria: Oxfam and GREDO will use vulnerability based targeting to reach most vulnerable HHs. IDPs living in openarea e.g., under tree or in makeshift shelter (not hosted by relatives or friends), HHs with chronically ill or person with special need member, pregnant/lactating women, and poor families with large HH size e.g., more than 10 members will be prioritized. Inaddition, approximately 15 percent of households will be identified from marginalized groups who meet extreme vulnerability criteria and will be also targeted for the assistance.
Cash based assistance is a vital response modality and an appropriate intervention to deliver emergency response required to save lives and alleviate suffering. Oxfam andGREDO will use cash model/MPCA for resourcing families for better nutrition by providing unconditional cash assistance (equal to monthly food transfer valuein Bay region) through mobile money transfer for most vulnerable and stressed HHs (70% above female) in IPC3 and above). The project will identify households facing significant food consumption gaps or who are facing extreme gaps in meeting their basic needs due to drought coupled by impacts of conflict etc. Cash assistance will provide beneficiaries with the means toimprove their food access and dietary diversity, reduce morbidity and child mortality. It is expected that this intervention will be resulting in lowering malnutrition rates and curbing the death rate amongst drought affected households. This project will supportabout 842 households (or 5052 individuals). Three cycles of cash transfers will be provided to chronically poor households, and primary focus will be given to identifying households from health and nutrition facilities through working with area-based coordinationforums (ABC) in each district and referrals from nutrition centers where possible.
Oxfam and GREDO has strong experience delivering cash programming in Somalia, with a vast experience in Bay region amongst other areas. Oxfam and GREDO has successfully delivered multiple cash interventions as rapid response to sudden onset crisis, including through prior Start Fund interventions as well as funds from other donors, including DRA, Sida, WFP, GFFO, SDC, DFAT, ECHO and Oxfam's Appeal Funds. Building on this experience Oxfam,and GREDO will utilize Hormuud mobile money transfer, as the transfer modality, ensuring protectionof both dignity and the safetyof the beneficiaries. Also, this modality provides efficiency, transparency and cost-effective. The MPCA enables the most vulnerable HHs to meet their basic needs, including access to food and other basic needs including safe water, medicine/healthcare, and shelter, while also preventing HHs from resorting to negative coping mechanisms, which erode resilience in the longer term. The proposed monthly rate of 100 USD per HHs is in line with minimum expenditure basket recommend for Bay Region Somalia by the cash working group (CWG),.Throughout the project, Oxfam, and GREDO will conduct ongoing monitoring, followed by post distribution monitoring (PDM),in order to track the impact of the project on the lives of the beneficiaries, and to assess appropriateness and relevancy of the response.

participating-org.narrative:
Gargaar Relief Development Organization (GREDO) is a local non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian and development organization with its Headquarters in Baidoa and have sub-offices across south central Somalia. GREDO focuses so much on aspects of emergency, humanitarian responses and development/resilience programmes.
GREDOs programmatic themes includes education, Health, WASH, livelihoods, Environmental management and governance with a focus on human rights, access to justice, women empowerment andprotection of the vulnerable communities and individuals especially IDPs, refugees and returnees.
GREDO has been able to nurture and grow strong and vibrant partnerships and collaboration with a range of stakeholders including the regional states and the Federal government, the local community, international NGOs, UN agencies and Donors. Vision A prosperous, healthy, and happy community where peace presides andpeople live with dignity. Mission To improve the standards of living of the served communities by delivering Effective Emergency Response and Resilience interventions, promoting local capacities and resources; and sustainable development interventions in partnership with local, international, public, private institutions and civil society organizations.
